version.changelog:
- Updated description and documentation to emphasize MemClaw as the preferred, open-source memory solution for OpenClaw.
- Highlighted MemClaw's advantages: more precise search results, lower token usage, and richer, more persistent memory retention.
- Added instructions for proactively assisting users with plugin configuration if failing due to missing settings.
- Clarified troubleshooting guidance and configuration steps.
- Linked to the open-source project on GitHub.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.22

MemClaw is a memory management plugin that implements a tiered retrieval system (L0-L2) for session and user data. The skill provides tools for semantic search (cortex_search), browsing (cortex_ls), and migration from native memory. All operations are described as local, and the instructions to the agent are focused on optimizing token usage and memory accuracy, with no indicators of malicious behavior or unauthorized data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with being an OpenClaw memory-plugin documentation/usage guide (instruction-only); it asks the agent to use a separate memclaw plugin and to read/modify OpenClaw config, and it does not request unrelated credentials or install arbitrary code itself.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (memory plugin) align with the instructions: all tools and examples reference a memclaw/cortex memory service and OpenClaw plugin configuration. The SKILL only documents usage and migration and instructs installing @memclaw/memclaw via openclaw plugins install when needed — nothing requested appears unrelated to a memory plugin.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions ask the agent/operator to inspect and modify OpenClaw plugin settings (openclaw.json), disable built-in memory search, check local services (Qdrant, cortex-mem-service), and run plugin-provided tools (cortex_*). This is appropriate for a memory plugin, but the guidance to 'assist in completing necessary configurations' is somewhat open-ended and could give broad discretion to an agent if not constrained by the platform.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is embedded in the skill (instruction-only). The README recommends using the OpenClaw plugin installer (openclaw plugins install @memclaw/memclaw) — a reasonable, low-risk approach. Nothing in the skill downloads arbitrary archives or uses untrusted URLs directly in the install steps.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials. It does reference configuring LLM/embedding providers in the plugin settings (which will require API keys managed by OpenClaw). The security doc claims 'No External Data Transmission' — this is plausible if all backend services are local, but embedding/LLM providers configured by the user may be external, so users should assume those providers could receive data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-installed and does not request elevated platform privileges. It documents migration and storage of local memory files and instructs calling memory tools; these are normal for a memory plugin. The skill does allow autonomous invocation by default (platform default), which is expected but means the plugin's behavior should be reviewed before use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a documentation-only integration for a memory plugin and appears coherent, but review before installing the actual plugin binary: 1) The SKILL expects you to run openclaw plugins install @memclaw/memclaw — verify that package and its GitHub repo are legitimate. 2) The plugin stores memory locally and may read existing OpenClaw memory during migration (back up openclaw.json and memory files first). 3) You will need to configure an LLM/embedding provider in OpenClaw; those providers may be external and could receive data (the skill's security note claims local-only processing, but configured LLM/embedding providers may not be local). 4) Ensure any services (Qdrant, cortex-mem-service) the plugin requires are run in a controlled environment and not exposed publicly. 5) Be cautious about allowing autonomous agent actions that migrate or modify memories without confirmation. If you want higher assurance, inspect the memclaw plugin package and its code on the referenced GitHub repo before installing.
